post.caption: Texas homeowners: it feels like every bill is going up. Electricity, for once, isn't. Residential power in Texas is 13.88 cents per kilowatt-hour — down 10.2% year over year (source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of 2026-08-01). We checked whether a mild summer explains it. It doesn't — cooling demand ran normal. The full read, with the numbers and where they came from → https://texashomeintelligence.com/analysis/are-texas-electricity-prices-still-going-up/ Send this to someone who's been told their bill only ever goes one way.
